title: Speculative decoding: performance or illusion?
gist: An independent study of speculative decoding variants inside a production engine, across workloads and batch sizes. Gains shrink as load rises and some variants fall below break-even; which method wins depends on the dataset.
changes: Cuts both ways. Fixed speculation is fragile under real load, which undercuts single-stream headline numbers. But an oracle choosing the method per token position does far better than any fixed choice, which is measured headroom for adaptivity.
caveats: The adaptive result assumes a perfect oracle. No practical predictor was built.

numbers.metric: One speculation method's speed-up as load rises
numbers.value: 1.73x at batch 1 falls to 1.21x at batch 128

numbers.metric: An oracle choosing the method per position

bears_on.note: The winning method changes with the dataset, the request and even the token position.
Speculation helps most at batch size 1, which is the single-user local case.
